transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, I'm here because... I guess things have just gotten really, really out of hand lately. I'm a teacher—I teach elementary school—so my days are just incredibly long and draining, you know, being "on" for the kids all day. And by the time I get home, I'm completely exhausted, but I still have all this work to do. But lately, well, I keep having these nights where I just... I eat an amount of food that honestly really scares me. 

Like, I'll be sitting there at my kitchen table, finishing up my grading for the night, and I'll tell myself I'm just going to have a little bit of the leftovers from dinner. Just a bite or two to get me through the rest of the math worksheets. But then I finish the leftovers, and it's like this switch flips in my brain, and I just can't stop. I'll go into the pantry and start going through boxes of cereal, just pouring it straight from the box, and then I'll move on to a whole sleeve of crackers, and then I'm just scooping peanut butter straight out of the jar. And it doesn't even stop there, I'll actually dig into my tote bag and eat whatever snacks I packed for my classroom—like the little granola bars and fruit snacks I keep for my students who forget their lunch. It’s like I just lose my mind and eat everything in sight, and I just keep going and going, and it’s terrifying because I don't even feel like myself when I'm doing it...
How do you feel after one of these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

Oh, God... I feel... I feel so much guilt and disgust, it's just overwhelming. It's like this heavy, suffocating blanket just drops on me the second I stop eating. I look at all the empty boxes and the wrappers scattered around the kitchen, and my stomach hurts so badly, it's stretched so tight, and I just think, "How could you do this again? You're a grown woman, you're a teacher, you should have some self-control." And the panic just sets in. I start calculating all the calories, the sheer volume of what I just put into my body, and I just feel so incredibly ashamed.

So, to try and fix it, to make up for what I've done... I'll tell myself I'm absolutely not allowed to eat anything the next day. I'll skip breakfast completely, which is hard because I usually need coffee and toast to get going, but I won't let myself have it. And then at school, during my lunch break—while all the other teachers are in the lounge eating their salads or whatever—I'll just sit in my classroom and grade papers or organize my lesson plans, and I won't eat a single bite. I'll tell them I have too much work to do or that I had a huge breakfast, but really I'm just trying to starve off all the damage from the night before. 

And then, as soon as the bell rings and the kids are gone, I don't even go home right away. I'll change into my workout clothes in the staff bathroom and I'll go straight to the running trail behind the school. And I will just run and run for hours. I'll tell myself I can't stop until I've burned it all off. Or I'll go to the gym and do these intense, two-hour hot yoga classes, and I'll push myself so hard. Even when my legs are literally shaking and I'm so dizzy and exhausted from not eating all day and just being on my feet teaching... I force myself to keep going. I just have to punish myself, I guess, and try to undo it, even though I'm so weak I can barely stand up by the end of it. It's just this endless, exhausting cycle, and I don't know how to stop.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food happen?

Um, gosh, if I really sit down and think about it... it’s been going on for a while now. I mean, for the past few months, especially since the school year really started picking up and the grading just became this absolute mountain on my desk... there has rarely been a week without at least one night where this happens. At least one night where I just completely lose it and eat far, far more than I ever meant to. 

And it's so frustrating because I'll start every single week on Monday morning telling myself, "Okay, this week is going to be different, you are going to be perfectly in control, you're just going to eat normal, healthy meals." But then, almost without fail, usually by Wednesday when the exhaustion is just peaking, I'm right back at the kitchen table surrounded by empty cereal boxes and wrappers. 

And then, because I did that, the very next day is just completely consumed by me trying to make up for it. I'll spend the entire next day just obsessing over how to undo the damage. Like I was saying, I'll go the whole day not eating at school, just sipping black coffee and making excuses to the other teachers about why I'm not in the breakroom for lunch. Or I'll force myself to push through a ridiculously long walk, just pounding the pavement on that trail behind the school until my feet actually ache, or I'll make myself do extra yoga on top of what I already do... just anything to burn it off. 

I just keep hoping that eventually I'll have a "good" week, a normal week where I don't do this, but for months now, there’s barely been a single week where I haven't had at least one of these nights followed by a day of just exhausting myself to fix it. It just takes over my whole schedule, you know? It's like I have a second full-time job on top of teaching, just managing this cycle...
When you restrict your food intake or exercise excessively after one of these episodes, is it specifically to prevent weight gain?

Yeah, yes, absolutely. It's... it's completely about the weight. I mean, the second I stop eating and look at the wrappers, the first thought in my head is always, "You are going to gain so much weight from this." And it just terrifies me. I've always been so careful about how I look, you know, being a teacher, you feel like everyone is looking at you, the parents, the administration, even the kids notice things. And the thought of going up a size, of my clothes not fitting right... it just sends me into a complete panic. 

So yeah, when I'm restricting the next day, when I'm telling myself I absolutely cannot have breakfast or lunch at school, it's 100% to stop the scale from moving. I'll sit in my classroom while everyone else is eating, and my stomach will be growling so loudly I'm worried the kids coming back from recess will hear it, but I just tell myself, "You have to do this, or you're going to get fat." 

And the exercise, too. It's not because I love running or because I want to be super fit. It's purely a transaction. I'm out on that trail for hours, or I'm pushing through that extra yoga class, even when I'm so shaky and exhausted I feel like I might actually pass out, just to burn off the calories. I'll literally try to calculate in my head how many miles I need to run to cancel out a sleeve of crackers, or how many minutes of hot yoga equals a bowl of cereal. It's exhausting, it really is, but I just can't bear the thought of gaining weight from what I did the night before. I have to undo it. I just have to.
